10 Οὕτω καὶ ὁ Κύριος ἡμῶν μέλλων ἐγείρειν ἐξ ᾅδου τὸν Λάζαρον, ἐδάκρυε μὲν ὁ φιλοικτίρμων καὶ κατεσπλαγχνίσθη, τὴν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου φύσιν φθειρομένην ὁρῶν καὶ τοῖς συνελθοῦσιν ἅμα σκυθρωπάζων, ἐνεβριμήσατο δὲ ἀοράτως τῷ κατέχοντι θανάτῳ καὶ φωνήσας ὁρατῶς τῷ κατεχομένῳ, τὸ μέγα τῆς οἰκείας
δυνάμεως ἀπεποίησε σημεῖον, τῆς καθόλου ἀναστάσεως ἐμφανίσας τὸν ἀρραβῶνα. ∆ιὰ τοῦτο συνανεκλίθη τῷ ποιηθέντι εὐφραινόμενος, ὡς πιστοποιήσας διὰ τῶν ἔργων ὅτι αὐτός ἐστιν «ἡ ζωὴ καὶ ἡ ἀνάστασις ἡμῶν»· προαναπεφώνητο γάρ που παρ' αὐτοῦ καὶ τοῦτο διὰ τοῦ προφήτου· «εὐφρανθήσομαι ἐν τῷ ἀγαθοποιεῖν με αὐτοῖς.» 11 Τῷδε τῷ θαύματι καὶ τῇ ἑαυτῶν ἑορτῇ αἱ τίμιαι μαθή τριαι τοῦ Σωτῆρος καὶ τοῦ ἀναστάντος ἀδελφαὶ διηκόνουν, ἡ μὲν τὰ τῆς ὑποδοχῆς, ἡ δὲ τὰ τῆς φιλοθεΐας προσκομίζουσαι. Ἦν γάρ πως ἡ Μάρθα φιλόξενος μὲν ὡς ἀβραμιαία, φιλόπτωχος δὲ ὡς ὁ Ἰὼβ, καὶ φιλόχριστος τὴν ὁμολογίαν ὡς Πέτρος, ἠνεῳγμένην ἔχουσα τὴν τῆς φιλοξενίας ἀγαπητικὴν θύραν παντὶ ἐρχομένῳ· ὅθεν οὐ λεληθότως, οὐδὲ ἐν ἀγνοίᾳ, ὡς πάλαι ὁ Λὼτ, ἀγγέλους ἐξένισεν, ἀλλ' ἐν εἰδήσει ἀγαθῇ καὶ διαθέσει τὸν τῶν ἀγγέλων δημιουργὸν καὶ κύριον ὑπὸ τὴν ὀροφὴν εἰσεδέξατο. Καὶ ἡ μὲν Μάρθα τοιαύτη καὶ τηλικαύτη καὶ ἐν τηλικούτοις. 12 Ἡ δὲ ταύτης ἀδελφὴ Μαρία καὶ αὐτὴ «λαβοῦσα λίτραν μύρου [νάρδου] πιστικῆς πολυτίμου ἤλειψεν τοὺς πόδας τοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ ταῖς θριξὶν αὐτῆς ἀπέμαξεν αὐτοῦ τοὺς πόδας, ἡ δὲ οἰκία ἐπλήσθη ἐκ τῆς ὀσμῆς τοῦ μύρου.» Μύρον εὐσεβείας πνέουσαι αἱ ἅγιαι, μύρου εὐωδίας καὶ τὴν οἰκίαν ἐπλήρωσαν, ἡ μὲν Μάρθα διὰ τῆς ὁμολογίας, ἡ δὲ Μαρία [διὰ] τῆς ἐργασίας. ∆εύτερος Πέτρος ἡ Μάρθα· ἐπέπνευσε γὰρ καὶ ταύτῃ ἡ χάρις καὶ διὰ τοῦτο αὐτὴ τὴν τοῦ κορυφαίου ἀνώμβρησε πίστιν. 13 Ἤκουσεν· «ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ κἂν ἀποθάνῃ, ζήσεται», ἐπέγνω τὸν τῆς ζωῆς χορηγὸν καὶ εὐθυβόλῳ χρησαμένη φωνῇ ἀνέκραγεν· «ἐγὼ πεπίστευκα ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὁ Χριστὸς ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ὁ εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἐρχόμενος.» Ἔδει γὰρ τὴν γυναικείαν φύσιν ἐπιγνῶναι καὶ ὁμολογῆσαι τὸν κτίστην καὶ θεόν. Πρῶτον Πέτρος θεοδιδάκτως ὁμολογεῖ, δεύτερον Μάρθα θεομυήτως ἀναφωνεῖ, τρίτον Ἰωάννης ἐν δέλτοις θεοφρόνως καὶ μονογενῶς θεολογεῖ. Πέτρος καὶ Μάρθα· «σὺ εἶ ὁ Χριστὸς ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος·» Ἰωάννης· «ἐν ἀρχῇ ἦν ὁ Λόγος καὶ ὁ Λόγος ἦν πρὸς τὸν θεὸν, καὶ θεὸς ἦν ὁ Λόγος. Καὶ ὁ Λόγος σὰρξ ἐγένετο καὶ ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν ἡμῖν.» 14 Πρόσεχε, ἀγαπητὲ, τῷ φωτισμῷ τῆς ἀληθείας, φεῦγε τὸ σκότος τῆς πλάνης. «Σὺ εἶ, φησὶν, ὁ Χριστός»· οὐ ψιλὸς Χριστὸς ἄνθρωπος, ἀλλ' υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος, ὁ Λόγος ὁ γενόμενος σὰρξ ἄτρεπτος δι' ἡμᾶς, ὁ μόνος υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος, ὁ Λόγος ὁ γενόμενος σάρξ· οὐχ εἷς τῶν Ἰουδαϊκῶν χριστῶν, οὐχ εἷς τῶν Ἰουδαϊκῶν καὶ παρεγγράπτων χριστῶν, ἀλλὰ σὺ κατὰ Παυλὸν, «ὁ εἷς Κύριος, ὁ ἐπὶ πάντων εὐλογητὸς εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, ἀμήν·» σὺ εἶ μόνος Χριστὸς καὶ υἱὸς μονογενὴς τοῦ θεοῦ, τοῦ ζῶντος· «ἐθεασάμεθα, φησὶν ὁ εὐαγγελιστὴς, τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, δόξαν ὡς μονογενοῦς παρὰ Πατρὸς, πλήρης χάριτος καὶ ἀληθείας·» 15 σὺ εἶ ὁ πρωτότοκος καὶ ὁ μονογενὴς καὶ μόνος σὺν ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι ὁμοούσιός τε καὶ ὁμότιμος καὶ ἰσοδύναμος τῷ γεγεννηκότι, ἄναρχός τε καὶ συναΐδιος θεῷ Πατρί· σὺ εἶ ὁ Χριστὸς, οὐχ εἷς τῶν ὑπό σου κτισθέντων ἀοράτων καὶ λειτουργικῶν σου δυνάμεων, ἀλλὰ φυσικῶς υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος. «Οὐ πρέσβυς γὰρ οὐδὲ ἄγγελος, ἀλλ' αὐτὸς ὁ Κύριος, φησὶν, ὡς εἶπεν Ἡσαΐας, ἔσωσεν ἡμᾶς, ἔσωσεν αὐτούς·» ὥστε οὐκ εἰσὶν οἱ ἄγγελοι χριστοί· σὺ εἶ ὁ Χριστὸς τοῦτ' ἔστιν οὐκ ἄνθρωπος Χριστὸς, ἀλλὰ θεὸς Χριστὸς, θεὸς ἐνανθρωπήσας, οὐκ ἄνθρωπος ἀποθεωθεὶς, ἀλλὰ χρίσας τὴν οἰκείαν καὶ ἑκούσιον σάρκωσιν τῇ οἰκείᾳ θεότητι δι' ὃ καὶ εἴρηται· «μῦρον ἐκκενωθὲν ὄνομά σου,» καὶ «εἰς ὀσμὴν μύρων σου ἐκδραμούμεθα·» σὺ εἶ ὁ Χριστὸς ὁ παρὰ πάσης κτίσεως προσκυνούμενος, ὡς εἷς Κύριος καὶ θεὸς, ὡς εἷς Υἱὸς, ὡς εἷς ∆εσπότης σὺν Πατρὶ [καὶ] τῷ ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι. 16 Πάλιν ἐπανάξωμεν τὸν λόγον ἐπὶ τὴν καλλίστην ἀδελφότητα τῶν εὐσεβῶν καὶ πιστῶν ἀδελφῶν. Ὦ συμπνοίας τῶν φίλων καὶ θεραπόντων γνησίων Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἑνὸς τῆς ἀκτίστου καὶ ὁμοουσίου Τριάδος.
thought_title: Martha confesses Christ and Mary anoints his feet
orientation: The preacher has shown Lazarus at table as proof of a real resurrection and now presents Martha and Mary in confession and love of God.
pass_a_gloss: So also our Lord, being about to raise Lazarus from Hades, wept, the compassionate one, and was moved in inward parts, seeing the nature of the human being being corrupted and at the same time sharing gloom with those who had come together, but he rebuked invisibly the death that holds sway and, having cried out visibly to the one held fast, he accomplished the great sign of his own power, displaying the pledge of the universal resurrection. For this reason he reclined at table together with the one who had been made, rejoicing, as having confirmed by his deeds that he himself is our life and our resurrection; for this also had been shouted beforehand by him through the prophet somewhere: I shall rejoice in doing good to them. To this marvel and to their own feast the honored women learners of the Savior and sisters of the one who had been resurrected ministered, the one bringing forward the things of reception, the other the things of love of God. For Martha was in a certain way hospitable in the manner of Abraham, a lover of the poor as Job was, and a lover of Christ in confession as Peter was, holding the loving door of hospitality opened to everyone who comes; for which reason not unnoticed nor in ignorance, as once Lot did, did she entertain angels, but with good knowledge and resolve she received under the roof the maker and lord of angels. And Martha was such and so great and in such great things. But Mary her sister herself also, having taken a pound of genuine and very costly nard ointment, anointed the feet of Jesus and wiped his feet with her hair, and the house was filled from the scent of the ointment. Breathing ointment of piety, the holy women also filled the house with ointment of sweet scent, Martha by confession, Mary by deed. Martha is a second Peter; for grace breathed upon her also and for this reason she showered upon us the faith of the foremost. She heard: the one who believes in me, even if he dies, shall live, she recognized the giver of life and, having used a straight shooting voice, cried out: I have believed that you are the Christ the son of God who comes into the world. For it was needful that female nature should know and confess the maker and God. First Peter confesses as taught by God, second Martha shouts as initiated by God, third John in writings thinks with the mind of God and speaks of God and of the Only Begotten. Peter and Martha say: you are the Christ the son of the living God; John says: in the beginning was the Word and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us. Attend, beloved, to the illumination of the truth, flee the darkness of error. You are, he says, the Christ; not a bare human Christ, but son of the living God, the Word who became flesh unchanged for our sake, the only son of the living God, the Word who became flesh; not one of the Jewish christs, not one of the Jewish and falsely enrolled christs, but you according to Paul, the one Lord, the one blessed over all into the ages of the ages, amen; you are alone Christ and only begotten son of God, of the living one; we beheld, says the evangelist, his glory, glory as of an only begotten from a Father, full of grace and truth; you are the firstborn and the only begotten and alone with the holy Spirit consubstantial and of equal honor and of equal power with the one who begot, without beginning and together eternal with God the Father; you are the Christ, not one of the invisible and serving powers made by you, but son of the living God by nature. For not an elder nor an angel, but the Lord himself, as Isaiah said, saved us, saved them; so angels are not christs; you are the Christ that is not a human Christ, but a divine Christ, God having undergone incarnation, not a human being made divine, but having anointed his own willing becoming flesh with his own divinity, on account of which also it has been said: your name is ointment poured out, and we shall run after the scent of your ointments; you are the Christ worshiped by all creation, as one Lord and God, as one Son, as one Master with the Father and the holy Spirit. Let us bring back again our account to the most beautiful brotherhood of the pious and faithful brothers. O harmony of the friends and genuine servants of Christ Jesus, one of the uncreated and consubstantial Trinity.

pass_b_english: So our Lord did the same when he was about to raise Lazarus from Hades. The compassionate one wept and was moved to his depths as he watched our mortal humanity wasting away, and he grieved together with the crowd that had gathered. Unseen he rebuked death that held Lazarus fast, and visibly he called to the one who was held, and so he worked the great sign of his own power. In it he set before our eyes the pledge of the universal resurrection. That is why he gladly reclined at table with the man he had made, proving by his deeds that he himself is our life and our resurrection. For he had already proclaimed this through the prophet: "I will rejoice in doing them good."

At this marvel and at their own feast, the honored women who learned from the Savior, the sisters of the risen man, served him, one bringing the gifts of welcome and the other the gifts of love for God. For Martha was hospitable like Abraham, generous to the poor like Job, and devoted to Christ in her confession like Peter, and she kept the loving door of welcome open to everyone who came. So she did not entertain angels by surprise and without knowing it, as Lot once did. With full knowledge and a ready heart she received under her roof the maker and Lord of angels. Such was Martha, so great and proven in such great things.

Her sister Mary then, as John the Evangelist says, "took a pound of very costly genuine nard ointment and anointed the feet of Jesus and wiped his feet with her hair, and the house was filled with the fragrance of the ointment" (John 12:3). The holy women breathed the ointment of devotion and filled the house with the sweet scent of ointment, Martha by her confession and Mary by her deed. Martha is a second Peter. Grace breathed upon her too, and so she poured forth the faith of the chief apostle.

She had heard Jesus say, "Whoever believes in me, even if he dies, will live" (John 11:25). She recognized the giver of life, and with a sure and piercing voice she cried out, "I believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God who comes into the world" (John 11:27). It was necessary for womankind to know and confess the Creator and God. First Peter confesses as taught by God, then Martha cries out as initiated by God, then John theologizes in his writings with a godly mind in the manner of the Only-begotten. Peter and Martha say together, "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God" (Matthew 16:16). And John says, "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God" (John 1:1). "And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us" (John 1:14).

Mark this, dear reader, the illumination of the truth, and flee the darkness of error. "You are," it says, "the Christ"—not a mere human Christ, but the Son of the living God, the Word become flesh unchanged for us, the only Son of the living God, the Word become flesh. He is not one of the Jewish anointed figures, not one of the Jewish and counterfeit anointed figures. In the words of Paul, you are "the one Lord, blessed over all for ages of ages, amen." You alone are Christ and only-begotten Son of the living God. As the Evangelist says, "We beheld his glory, glory as of the only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth" (John 1:14).

You are the firstborn and the only-begotten, and alone with the Holy Spirit you are consubstantial and equally honored and equally mighty with the one who begot you, without beginning and coeternal with God the Father. You are the Christ, not one of the unseen ministering powers you created, but Son of the living God by nature. For, as Isaiah said, "No envoy and no angel, but the Lord himself saved us, he saved them" (Isaiah 63:9). So angels are not christs. You are the Christ, which means not a human Christ but a divine Christ, God incarnate, not a man made divine, but one who, having anointed his own willing becoming flesh with his own divinity, is rightly addressed, "Your name is ointment poured out," and "we will run after the fragrance of your ointments" (Song of Songs 1:3–4). You are the Christ whom all creation worships as one Lord and God, as one Son, as one Master with the Father and the Holy Spirit.

Let us turn our speech back again to that most beautiful fellowship of siblings, the devout and faithful brother and sisters. What harmony among the friends and true servants of Christ Jesus, one of the uncreated and consubstantial Trinity.
notes: The source shows added words in square brackets at nard, deed, and Father, read them as supplied and not as certain.

problems.quote: is rightly addressed, "Your name is ointment poured out" (Song of Songs 1:3).
problems.source_quote: «μῦρον ἐκκενωθὲν ὄνομά σου,» καὶ «εἰς ὀσμὴν μύρων σου ἐκδραμούμεθα·»
problems.why: Omits the second Song of Songs quotation ('and we will run after the fragrance of your ointments').
problems.fix: is rightly addressed, "Your name is ointment poured out," and "we will run after the fragrance of your ointments" (Song of Songs 1:3–4).

problems.quote: that most beautiful pair, the devout and faithful brother and sisters.
problems.source_quote: τὴν καλλίστην ἀδελφότητα τῶν εὐσεβῶν καὶ πιστῶν ἀδελφῶν.
problems.why: Renders ἀδελφότητα ('brotherhood/siblinghood') as 'pair', contradicting the three siblings (Lazarus, Martha, and Mary) named right after.
problems.fix: that most beautiful fellowship of siblings, the devout and faithful brother and sisters.

problems.quote: with a voice all could hear he called to the one death held
problems.why: ὁρατῶς means visibly, paired with the unseen rebuke of death, not audibly.
problems.fix: Unseen he rebuked the death that held him, and visibly he called to the one who was held.
problems.ruling: ὁρατῶς means 'visibly,' paired with ἀοράτως ('invisibly'); rendering it 'with a voice all could hear' shifts sight to sound and loses the antithesis.

problems.quote: with a sure and piercing voice Origen says she cried out
problems.why: Martha herself cries out. Origen is not named and does not speak.
problems.fix: and with a well-aimed voice she cried out, "I believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God who comes into the world."
problems.ruling: Source εὐθυβόλῳ χρησαμένη φωνῇ ἀνέκραγεν has Martha crying out directly; 'Origen says' is a hallucinated insertion absent from the Greek.

problems.quote: No elder and no angel, but the Lord himself saved us, he saved them
problems.source_quote: Οὐ πρέσβυς γὰρ οὐδὲ ἄγγελος, ἀλλ' αὐτὸς ὁ Κύριος... ἔσωσεν ἡμᾶς, ἔσωσεν αὐτούς
problems.why: Beside ἄγγελος, πρέσβυς means envoy or messenger, not an elder.
problems.fix: "No envoy and no angel, but the Lord himself saved us; he saved them."
problems.ruling: In Isaiah 63:9 LXX, πρέσβυς paired with ἄγγελος means 'envoy' or 'ambassador,' not 'elder,' which misleads and breaks the intermediary parallel.

problems.quote: with a sure and piercing voice Origen says she cried out,
problems.why: Adds 'Origen says', which does not appear in the Greek and falsely attributes the narrative to Origen.
problems.fix: with a sure and piercing voice she cried out,
problems.ruling: Greek has only εὐθυβόλῳ χρησαμένη φωνῇ ἀνέκραγεν; “Origen says” is absent and misattributes the cry.

problems.quote: When Martha says, "You are the Christ," she does not mean a mere human Christ. She means the Son of the living God
problems.source_quote: «Σὺ εἶ, φησὶν, ὁ Χριστός»· οὐ ψιλὸς Χριστὸς ἄνθρωπος, ἀλλ' υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος
problems.why: The denial of a mere human Christ is the preacher's address to Christ, not Martha's own gloss.
problems.fix: "You are," it says, "the Christ"—not a mere human Christ, but the Son of the living God.
problems.ruling: Greek «Σὺ εἶ, φησὶν, ὁ Χριστός» begins the preacher's address to Christ (ἀλλὰ σὺ), not Martha's gloss ("she does not mean... She means").

problems.quote: the one of the uncreated and consubstantial Trinity
problems.source_quote: ἑνὸς τῆς ἀκτίστου καὶ ὁμοουσίου Τριάδος
problems.why: Anarthrous ἑνὸς means "one of" (one Person of the Trinity); adding "the" distorts the Trinitarian formula and makes it sound singular or ungrammatical.
problems.fix: one of the uncreated and consubstantial Trinity
problems.ruling: Anarthrous ἑνὸς τῆς … Τριάδος is partitive “one of the Trinity”; “the one of” adds an article and misreads the formula.

[mistranslation] real error: anarthrous ἑνὸς τῆς...Τριάδος means one Person of the Trinity; removed added 'the'.
[earlier] ointment quotes: no edit — English already has both source quotes μῦρον ἐκκενωθὲν ὄνομά σου + εἰς ὀσμὴν μύρων σου ἐκδραμούμεθα.
[earlier] fellowship of siblings: no edit — English already renders ἀδελφότητα τῶν...ἀδελφῶν as fellowship, not pair.
[earlier] Unseen/visibly: no edit — English already matches ἀοράτως / ὁρατῶς and τῷ κατεχομένῳ.
[earlier] she cried out: no edit — English already matches εὐθυβόλῳ...φωνῇ ἀνέκραγεν with no Origen.

problems.quote: It was fitting for a woman to know and confess the creator and God.
problems.source_quote: Ἔδει γὰρ τὴν γυναικείαν φύσιν ἐπιγνῶναι καὶ ὁμολογῆσαι τὸν κτίστην καὶ θεόν.
problems.why: ἔδει is necessity, and γυναικείαν φύσιν is womankind, not one woman.
problems.fix: It was necessary that womankind recognize and confess the Creator and God.
problems.ruling: τὴν γυναικείαν φύσιν means female nature or womankind, not 'a woman', and ἔδει expresses necessity rather than mere fittingness.

problems.quote: then John theologizes with godly mind in his writings about the only Son.
problems.source_quote: τρίτον Ἰωάννης ἐν δέλτοις θεοφρόνως καὶ μονογενῶς θεολογεῖ.
problems.why: μονογενῶς is an adverb of manner, parallel to θεοφρόνως, not the topic of the writings.
problems.fix: Then John, in his writings, theologizes with a godly mind and in an only-begotten manner.
problems.ruling: μονογενῶς is a manner adverb coordinated with θεοφρόνως modifying θεολογεῖ ('uniquely/singularly'), not a topic phrase 'about the only Son'.

edits.old: It was fitting for a woman to know and confess the creator and God.
edits.new: It was necessary for womankind to know and confess the Creator and God.

edits.old: then Martha cries out as initiated by God, then John theologizes with godly mind in his writings about the only Son.
edits.new: then Martha cries out as initiated by God, then John theologizes in his writings with a godly mind in the manner of the Only-begotten.

fixed: Fixed to necessity + womankind: source Ἔδει = it was necessary, not fitting, and την γυναικειαν φυσιν = female nature/womankind, not one woman.
Fixed to manner, not topic: source μονογενως parallels θεοφρονως as adverbs of manner for θεολογει, not 'about the Son'; rendered naturally as 'in the manner of' rather than stiff literal adverb.

last_rejected.quote: For he had already proclaimed this through the prophet: "I will rejoice in doing them good."
last_rejected.source_quote: εὐφραινόμενος, ὡς πιστοποιήσας διὰ τῶν ἔργων ὅτι αὐτός ἐστιν «ἡ ζωὴ καὶ ἡ ἀνάστασις ἡμῶν»· προαναπεφώνητο γάρ που παρ' αὐτοῦ καὶ τοῦτο διὰ τοῦ προφήτου· «εὐφρανθήσομαι ἐν τῷ ἀγαθοποιεῖν με αὐτοῖς.»
last_rejected.why: The prophecy explains his rejoicing in doing good, not that he is life and resurrection. “Somewhere” is also dropped.
last_rejected.fix: He reclined rejoicing, proving by his deeds that he is our life and resurrection. Somewhere he had already said through the prophet, “I will rejoice in doing them good.”
last_rejected.ruling: Like Greek τοῦτο before the quote, English 'this:' points forward to the quotation; omitting που ('somewhere') is minor, not a major error.
